messages:
maria: Heads up — prod-host-22 hit an OOM during a long-context job (~1.1M tokens). Heap didn't shrink even after multiple evict/paging cycles. Dumped a few traces, looks fragmentation-y.

alex: ugh. which subsystem? kv cache or general heap?

maria: KV cache. We saw continuous evict attempts but free_slots stayed near zero and fragments spiked. Paging kicked in and then the OOM killer.

jon: Can you paste the short log snippet?

maria: Sure — here's the tail:

```
KVCache: shard=7 evict_attempts=34 free_slots=1 fragments=312 reclaimable_bytes=18MB
KVCache: shard=7 page_out=4096 page_in=0 reuse_miss=89
KernelSelector: switched->int8-fast (workspace=1.9GB)
OOM: process redwood-runtime pid=24123 killed
```

sara: Important: reclaimable_bytes is tiny vs total memory. Sounds like lots of small fragmented slabs that can't be coalesced by current allocator.

alex: This matches a repro I hit locally — long dialogs keep allocating many short-lived KV slices and compaction isn't aggressive enough. Our current compaction runs only on low-pressure idle windows.

elaine: Could be interacting with kernel selection too — we picked a kernel with bigger workspace which amplified memory pressure during generation. Maybe prefer a kernel with smaller peak working set for long contexts.

jon: Agreed. Short-term mitigations? We need an on-host graceful fallback so the request doesn't hard OOM. Ideas: preemptive per-shard compaction probe, soft-evict with retry/backoff, and a kv-less path (serve but without KV cache) as last resort.

alex: Proposal: add a "reclaim hint probe" that scans frag histograms when evicts fail > N times and tries to coalesce small fragments into a reclaimable slab. If that probe doesn't free > X, trigger fallback. Cheap to implement (allocator-level) and togglable.

maria: I like the probe name. Also add a quick policy: after M failed evict retries, pick most-recent request and try a partial KV prune (drop older prefixes, keep last K utterances). That should bound memory use for very long contexts.

sara: For immediate deploy: (1) increase evict aggressiveness threshold on hosted pool for safety, (2) enable a telemetry flag to capture frag histograms and reuse_miss rates, (3) add a user-visible graceful degrade response when we fall back to kv-less path.

jon: Who owns the telemetry flag? alex?

alex: I'll add the flag and dashboard tiles. Will emit histograms: frag_bucket_counts, reclaimable_bytes, evict_retries, kernel_workspace_bytes.

elaine: I'll prototype kernel selection change: add a long-context hint that biases towards kernels with smaller peak workspace even if marginally slower. We keep the current for short requests.

maria: For the correctness side: ensure dropping older prefixes doesn't break deterministicness for reruns. We should only do that for best-effort mode and log a specific trace ID so users can correlate.

alex: Quick code snippet for the probe we discussed (pseudo):

```
if (evict_retries > 8) {
  scan_fragments(shard);
  coalesce_small_fragments(<=64B);
  if (freed < 16MB) {
    mark_request_for_kvless_fallback(req_id);
  }
}
```

jon: Nice. Add exponential backoff so we don't thrash the allocator. Also ensure we don't run this during normal GC windows.

sara: Can we add a server-side circuit breaker that flips to a lower-memory model variant (int8-dropcache) for the whole host when frag rate crosses a threshold? That would be a blunt but safe fallback.

elaine: Yes — model variant switch is doable but requires quick rollout and verification. We need canary and fast rollback. deploy-bot, can we schedule a canary job?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deployment to prod-host-22 at 02:00 UTC. Canary window: 30m. Rollback on error >=3 or OOM event.

maria: Action items: alex = telemetry + evict counters (ETA 24h), elaine = kernel-selection long-ctx hint + small canary (ETA 48h), jon = implement reclaim-hint probe + partial-prune fallback (ETA 72h), sara = public degrade message & tests (ETA 48h). I'll own postmortem and follow-up.

alex: I'll also add a lightweight test that simulates many small KV allocations over long sequences to regress-test frag growth.

sara: Also add an integration test for the kv-less path so we verify responses degrade gracefully (return header x-redwood-kv-fallback: true).

jon: One more thought — batching heuristics: if a batch contains many long-context requests, we should cap batch size dynamically to reduce aggregate workspace peaks. I'll add a heuristic: batch_cost = sum(estimated_workspace(req_i)); cap when > host_limit.

maria: Good call. That will avoid pathological kernel workspace growth from combining many long sessions.

elaine: Ok I'm pairing with alex tomorrow to align telemetry with kernel selector signals.

maria: Thanks all — let's treat this as P1 until the canary proves stable. Will update timeline in #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
